meta.unit: chain-layer decoder gates: exact-height equality on numbered reads (F1) and presence-tracked required fields (F2) — the response must answer the question asked
meta.purpose: Task 9 wave 6 brief's mutation requirement: the height-equality check (W6M1 deletes it — the buggy-proxy defect Codex round 5 named as [high]), each required-field presence check (W6M2 hash, W6M3 parentHash, W6M4 number, W6M5 timestamp — W6M5 IS the round-5 [medium] F2 defect restored: an absent timestamp decoding as the Unix epoch), and the null-vs-violation discrimination (W6M6 misclassifies an honest not-found as a protocol violation; W6M7 fabricates a header from the null result). Run through the wave-16 committed applier (.superpowers/sdd/wave16-mutations/mutate.py): exactly-one-occurrence asserted per edit, byte-level backups, in-memory restores verified byte-identical. chain.go is CRLF in the working tree, so multi-line patterns embed \r\n explicitly.
design_notes: EVERY MUTANT LIVES INSIDE validateReportedHeader — the wave-6 rule's single enforcement site. The raw-JSON fixture layer (chain_rawjson_test.go) reaches it through the REAL decode (Dial -> rpc.Client -> endpointClient -> gate), so these mutants are killable from BELOW the fake seam as well as through it; the transcript's kill lists record both fronts.

W6M2 (hash presence) IS A MESSAGE-LEVEL KILL, disclosed: an absent hash backfilled to a zero value is still refused one line later by the wave-5 zero-hash gate, so rotation behavior is identical either way — the observable difference is the violation's NAME ('omits required field(s) hash' vs 'reports a zero hash'). That name is the property: a decoder that misreports absence as a reported zero value is the F2 lie one level up, and the regression tests assert the absence surfaces AS absence. No stronger observable exists because the zero gate deliberately dominates.

W6M3/W6M4/W6M5 ARE BEHAVIORAL KILLS: under each, the malformed primary's attempt SUCCEEDS (parentHash/number/timestamp backfilled), so the regression tests see a value handed out where they assert a violation-plus-rotation — W6M4 additionally models the echo-chamber defect (the decoder answering the height question FOR the provider, which makes the F1 equality gate pass vacuously), and W6M5 restores the exact production shape round 5 described: HeaderTime returning the Unix epoch and failover stopping at the malformed primary.

W6M4's guard is `rh.Number == nil && want != nil`: on the head path (want nil) the mutant leaves Number nil and the later IsUint64 deref would panic — no test drives that composition (the missing-number regressions are numbered reads, where the mutant vacuously passes the equality gate and dies by assertion), disclosed so a future reader does not mistake the guard for coverage.

W6M6 AND W6M7 TARGET THE SAME SEARCH TEXT (the nil-header arm) with different lies — misclassification vs fabrication. They are separate mutants applied and restored independently, so the exactly-once assertion holds for each; together they pin both faces of the discrimination: a null result for a beyond-head block is a LEGITIMATE not-found that must surface as such, never as a protocol violation (W6M6) and never as a header for the gates to judge (W6M7).

THE PRICES SUITE IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND to every mutant here (fakePollChain fakes the PollChain seam above the Failover). W6M5 includes ./internal/prices/ anyway so the transcript records that blindness — the W4M4/W5M3 precedent; the freshness/staleness composition is pinned from the chain side by the HeaderTime and HeadFrom regressions.

SOLVENT_LIVE_RPC_TESTS stays UNSET for every mutation run (no public-endpoint hammering inside a loop; the live regression's gated SKIP is its designed hermetic-run state). TEST_DATABASE_URL points at solvent_t9w1 so nothing DB-gated skips in the W6M5 prices run. The raw-JSON layer needs no gate: its JSON-RPC servers are local httptest instances.

mutations.description: the height-equality gate is deleted: numbered reads accept a well-formed answer for ANY height
mutations.property: EXACT-HEIGHT EQUALITY ON EVERY NUMBERED READ (F1, round-5 [high]): a well-formed response for the wrong height — a proxy answering latest for numeric requests — is a protocol violation that fails the attempt and rotates; it can never date HeaderTime's freshness measurement or feed walker ancestry a hash for a block nobody asked about

edits.replace: // MUTANT W6M1: numbered reads accept a well-formed answer for ANY height

mutations.description: the hash presence check backfills: an absent hash silently becomes a zero value for the zero gate to judge
mutations.property: ABSENCE SURFACES AS ABSENCE (F2, hash): a response omitting the hash field is refused as 'omits required field(s) hash' — a decoder that backfills a plausible zero value misreports what the provider actually said, which is the F2 lie one level up (kill is at the violation's NAME; rotation is identical either way because the zero-hash gate dominates — disclosed in design notes)

mutations.description: the parentHash presence check backfills: an absent parentHash silently becomes a zero value and the read succeeds
mutations.property: PRESENCE-TRACKED parentHash (F2): a response omitting parentHash is a protocol violation that fails the attempt — under the mutant the read SUCCEEDS with a fabricated zero parent, handing reorg ancestry a lineage the provider never reported

mutations.description: the number presence check echoes: an absent number is backfilled with the height the caller asked for
mutations.property: PRESENCE-TRACKED number (F2) AND THE ECHO-CHAMBER GUARD ON F1: an absent number is a violation in its own right — a decoder that backfills it with the height asked makes the exact-height gate pass vacuously, 'verifying' the response against an answer the decoder itself invented

mutations.description: the timestamp presence check backfills: an absent timestamp decodes as the Unix epoch — the round-5 F2 defect restored
mutations.property: PRESENCE-TRACKED timestamp (F2, round-5 [medium], the incident shape): an omitted timestamp is a protocol violation that fails the attempt so failover reaches a healthy secondary — under the mutant HeaderTime reports the Unix epoch and HeadFrom an epoch-aged head from the malformed primary, the false-stale composition that froze failover

mutations.description: the null result is misclassified: an honest not-found surfaces as a provider protocol violation
mutations.property: NULL-VS-VIOLATION DISCRIMINATION, face one: a null result for a beyond-head block is a LEGITIMATE not-found that must surface as such — misclassifying it as a protocol violation would put honest lagging endpoints in the same bucket as malformed ones and page operators for ordinary beyond-head reads

mutations.description: the null result is fabricated into an empty header for the downstream gates to judge
mutations.property: NULL-VS-VIOLATION DISCRIMINATION, face two: a null result is never fabricated into a header — under the mutant the empty header trips the presence gates and the not-found surfaces as a field-omission protocol violation, erasing the one honest answer a lagging endpoint gave
